input.title: DESIGN §8's force recipe produces an item no executor will ever pick
input.body:
Found by following the documented recipe on live traffic (#801 Step 3, GCEC #907).

§8 says:

> **Forcing a scheduled task is waking its standing item** … force = strip `task:blocked`, clear `Not-before`, optionally add `task:urgent`

Followed literally, that leaves an item carrying neither `task:blocked` nor `task:ready`. `pickOrder` filters on `hasLabel(i, READY)` ([`queue/executor.mjs:58`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L58)) — `task:urgent` only affects the **sort**, never admission. So the forced item is invisible to every executor, and the tick will not rescue it either: its ready job transitions `task:blocked → task:ready`, and the item no longer carries `task:blocked`.

Observed exactly that on GoogleCalendarEventCreator: forced `core/update` (#907) at 11:11Z, the `task:urgent` label event fired the executor within seconds, and [the run](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/actions/runs/31943656688) logged `- nothing ready to pick up` and exited clean. A silent no-op that looks exactly like a healthy run — the failure mode §8 is otherwise careful about ("a force that finds no work *says so* where the operator will read it"). Here it says nothing to the item at all.

The engine's own re-queue instruction has it right — *"remove `needs-human`, add `task:ready`"* ([`executor.mjs:326`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L326)) — so this is a prose defect, not a code one. §8 frames force and the §4 human re-queue as "the same operation on the same object", which is true, and then spells only one of them correctly.

**Fix:** §8's recipe becomes *strip `task:blocked`, add `task:ready`, clear `Not-before`, optionally add `task:urgent`*, matching §4. Worth checking whether the simulator has a scenario for forcing a blocked standing item, since S-coverage would have caught the divergence if the recipe were pinned anywhere executable.

Small enough to fold into the next #801 change rather than carry alone.

input.title: A needs-human park leaves its claim standing, so the item livelocks forever once re-queued
input.body:
Caught on live traffic doing exactly what the engine's own message instructs. #801 Step 3, B7's second half.

## The throwing call site

[`queue/executor.mjs:92-99`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L92) — `claimWinner`:

```js
const boundary = sorted.filter((c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(EPISODE_MARKER)).at(-1);
const claims = sorted
  .filter((c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(CLAIM_MARKER))
  .filter((c) => !boundary || c.id > boundary.id);
return claims[0] ?? null;
```

With no `EPISODE_MARKER` anywhere on the item, `boundary` is `undefined`, the filter is a no-op, and `claims[0]` is the **oldest claim the item ever received**. Every later executor claims the item, reads back a claim that is not its own, logs `another executor holds this episode's earliest claim — moving on`, and drops it — leaving the item `task:executing` with nobody executing. The tick's executing-leash reclaim returns it to `task:ready` ~1h later and the cycle repeats. Forever.

The comment block immediately above that function names this exact hazard and states the invariant it depends on:

> Over an item's lifetime dead claims accumulate … arbitrating over all of them makes a dead claim outrank every future live claimant — the item then livelocks through reclaim cycles forever. **The reclaim / revert / re-queue comment is the boundary.**

## Which side fails to hold it up

Three paths post the marker — the tick's reclaim ([`tick.mjs:230`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/tick.mjs#L230)), the F15 revert ([`executor.mjs:174`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L174)), and the hand-wake ([`create-work-item.mjs:64`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/create-work-item.mjs#L64)).

The **`needs-human` park does not**. It posts a plain comment and stops ([`executor.mjs:326`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L326)) — and that comment is the *instruction to re-queue*:

> No session was started. Fix the invocation endpoint, then re-queue this item (remove `needs-human`, add `task:ready`).

Follow it exactly and you get a permanently unclaimable item. The engine tells you to do the thing that breaks it.

## Observed

GoogleCalendarEventCreator #908 (`grow_with_claudinite/growth-dedup`):

| | |
|---|---|
| 04:55:30Z | claimed by `actions-31927761001` |
| 04:55:53Z | parked `needs-human` — no endpoint configured. **Claim comment left standing** |
| 11:14:12Z | re-queued per the printed instruction: `needs-human` off, `task:ready` on |
| 11:14:26Z | claimed by `actions-31943780210` |
| 11:14:27Z | [same run](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/actions/runs/31943780210) loses to the 04:55 claim and moves on — it lost the race to itself |

Unblocked by hand by posting the marker and re-readying.

## Fix

The `needs-human` park is a terminal convergence of the episode, so it belongs in the same class as reclaim and revert: post `EPISODE_MARKER` when parking. Then the printed instruction stays true as written and no operator has to know the marker exists.

Worth checking the other terminal paths for the same omission, and pinning it with a test that re-queues a parked item and asserts the next claim wins — a single-claim test cannot see this, which is why the whole burst missed it (the `basics/writing-tests` rule about calling a helper twice across a re-queue is exactly this shape).

Ties into #892: both are terminal-convergence side effects that a session or a park is trusted to perform and doesn't.

## Wider than the park — the **roll** leaks the same way, and canon has been paying for it since the flip

The roll exit is the one that deliberately writes no comment ([`executor.mjs:244`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs#L244)):

> The roll writes no comment — the `Not-before` bump IS the record, and an hourly task that stays quiet would otherwise fill its own timeline (§5).

Correct as a spam decision, and it leaves the claim standing too. So a rolled item's next claim also loses to a dead one.

**This is not hypothetical — it is on canon #860 right now:**

| | |
|---|---|
| 15th 17:44:17Z | episode marker (hand wake) |
| 15th 17:44:39Z | claimed by `actions-31899161709` → precondition declined → **rolled**, no marker |
| 16th 02:11:27Z | claimed by `actions-31921280933` — loses to the 17:44 claim, moves on. Item left `task:executing`, nobody executing |
| 16th 03:32:50Z | tick's 60-minute executing-leash reclaim fires, posts a marker |
| 16th 03:33:04Z | claimed by `actions-31924498191` — now the earliest after the boundary, wins, rolls correctly |

So every rolled item on the fleet costs **one wasted claim plus one full leash period** before it can run again. #860 sat unrunnable from 17:44Z to 03:32Z. The executing-leash reclaim is what recovers it, which is exactly why this reads as healthy from the outside — in this morning's recap I counted #860 as "correctly still blocked", and it was, just nine hours later than it should have been.

The two halves differ only in recovery: the roll self-heals in ≤1h, the `needs-human` park never does (nothing reclaims a parked item), so it livelocks until a human intervenes.

## Which makes the fix a design call, not a one-liner

Posting `EPISODE_MARKER` at the park site fixes the permanent half and is unarguable. The roll half cannot take the same treatment without reintroducing the per-roll timeline entry §5 removed on purpose — an hourly task would post one every hour.

The shape that satisfies both: **an executor relinquishing an item strikes its own claim** — append the marker to the claim comment it already wrote, rather than adding a new one. `claimWinner`'s boundary logic then excludes it naturally, there is no new timeline entry, and one mechanism covers roll, park, and a failed hand-off alike. Cost is one extra API call on exit paths that are already making several.

That trades the append-only comment log for an edit, which is a real change to what the arbitration artifact means, so it wants your call rather than mine. Alternatives if you'd rather not edit comments: a marker comment on roll (accepting the spam), or teaching `claimWinner` to treat a claim as void once the item has left `task:executing` (cheap, but re-derives state the comments were made the sole arbiter of on purpose).

Related: this is the third terminal-convergence side effect trusted to a caller that doesn't perform it (#892, and #883's durable record). Whatever `converge-item.mjs` ends up being is probably where all three land together.

content.text:
**The problem**

An executor claims an item by posting a claim comment. Whoever posted the *earliest* claim wins.

When an executor finishes with an item but doesn't close it — the precondition said "no work" (roll), or it parked the item as `needs-human` — it leaves its claim comment sitting there. Nothing marks it dead.

So the next executor to pick that item up posts its claim, looks for the earliest claim, and finds the **old dead one**. It concludes someone else owns the item and walks away. Nobody runs it.

There is already a mechanism for this: an `EPISODE_MARKER` comment acts as a line in the sand — claims before it don't count. The tick's reclaim posts one. The roll and the park don't.

**What it costs**

- **Roll**: recovers after 60 minutes, when the tick notices the "executing" item has gone silent and posts a marker. Canon #860 sat unrunnable from 17:44Z to 03:32Z last night for exactly this reason. Every rolled item on the fleet pays this.
- **Park**: never recovers. Nothing reclaims a parked item. GCEC #908 was stuck permanently until I posted a marker by hand.

**The options**

1. **Strike the claim** — when an executor lets go of an item, it edits its own claim comment to mark it spent. Covers both cases, adds no new comments. Downside: the comment log stops being append-only.

2. **Post a marker comment on every exit** — simple and keeps comments immutable, but the roll deliberately writes nothing today to avoid an hourly task spamming its own timeline. This brings that back.

3. **Ignore claims from before the item's last label change** — no comments involved at all. Cheapest. Downside: label state becomes part of arbitration, and right now it deliberately isn't — that's what makes a half-finished label swap harmless.

4. **Fix the park only** — post a marker where the item parks, since that's the half that never recovers. Leave the roll's hour of latency until #892's cleanup lands.

input.title: A losing claimant's own comment bumps updated_at, so contention postpones the leash reclaim it depends on
input.body:
Split out of #922 at the owner's direction — a latent issue the strike does **not** fix.

The tick's executing-leash reclaim keys on the item's activity clock, which is GitHub's `updated_at`. Every claim attempt posts a comment, and a comment bumps `updated_at` — including the attempt of an executor that goes on to *lose* the arbitration and walk away.

So on an item nobody is actually working, each losing claimant resets the clock the reclaim is counting down. The busier the queue, the more executors arrive, the further the recovery is pushed out. Under a `labeled`-event executor plus an hourly drain, an item can be re-touched often enough that the leash never elapses.

This is what made the observed stall on canon #860 ~10h rather than the ~1h the leash nominally promises: the failed claims kept the item looking alive.

#922 removes the *cause* of those repeated losing claims, so the common case goes away with it. What stays is the general property: whenever an executor genuinely dies mid-claim, any later claim attempt on that item defers its recovery. Contention postpones the mechanism that exists precisely to recover from failure.

Worth considering:
- read the last **heartbeat/claim by the current holder** as the activity clock, rather than the item's `updated_at` — the heartbeat work in #883 already introduces a per-holder liveness signal, which is the natural carrier;
- or have a losing claimant not write to the item at all, which needs a claim protocol that reads before it writes (a bigger change, and it trades away the property that makes the current one correct under a stale snapshot).

Not urgent — the failure needs a dead executor *and* ongoing contention on the same item — but it should not be discovered a second time from a stall.

Letting go of an open item kills your claim

F18 stated the episode boundary as a rule — "earliest claim since the item
last became ready" — and it was implemented over the three paths that
already wrote a comment. The two that end an episode silently were left
out: the roll, which is comment-free on purpose, and the needs-human park.
Both leave the claim standing, so the next claimant loses to a dead one.
The roll self-heals via the leash; the park never does, so a human
following the park's own re-queue instruction gets an item nothing can
ever claim.

The departing executor now strikes its own claim, appending the episode
marker to the comment it already wrote. That ends the episode without the
timeline entry a marker comment would cost, which is what lets the roll
use it. A losing claimant strikes too — its claim outlives the winner's
strike and would become the earliest of the next episode.

The simulator could not reproduce any of this: it advanced the epoch on
every transition into ready, encoding the rule's intent rather than the
artifact, so the silent paths looked correct there and livelocked in
production. It now advances the epoch only where the engine leaves a mark.

Fixes #922
Refs #801, #924

Fixes #922. Refs #801 (Step 3), #924.

## The defect

F18 stated the episode boundary semantically — *"earliest claim since the item last became ready"* — and it was implemented over the three paths that already wrote a comment: the reclaim, the F15 revert, the hand-wake. The two paths that end an episode **silently** were never covered:

- the **roll**, which is comment-free on purpose (§5: an hourly task that declines every hour must not fill its own timeline);
- the **`needs-human` park**.

Both leave the claim standing, so `claimWinner` finds no boundary and returns a dead claim. The next claimant loses to it. The roll self-heals in ≤1h via the leash reclaim; the park never does, because nothing reclaims a parked item — so a human following the park's *own* printed re-queue instruction (F7) gets an item nothing can ever claim.

Both were live: canon #860 sat unrunnable 17:44Z→03:32Z on the roll path, and GoogleCalendarEventCreator #908 livelocked on the park path until I posted a marker by hand.

## The fix

**Letting go of an open item kills your claim.** The departing executor appends the episode marker to the claim comment it already wrote, rather than posting a new one — which ends the episode at no timeline cost, and is what lets the roll use it.

Three sites: the roll, every `needs-human` park (`converge` is the single funnel, so all six call sites are covered), and a claimant that **lost** the arbitration. That last one is not in the original report and is the one that would have made a partial fix look complete: a loser's claim is *younger* than the winner's, so it survives the winner's strike and becomes the earliest claim of the *next* episode — moving the livelock one episode along instead of removing it.

A successful hand-off deliberately does not strike (that episode is live, owned by the session), and a dead executor strikes nothing, which is what the leash reclaim is for. The strike happens **before** the label swap, so a crash between them leaves `task:executing` with a spent claim — the state the leash already recovers — rather than the parked-and-unclaimable state this fixes.

## Why the simulator never caught it

`sim.mjs` advanced the claim epoch on **every transition into ready**, encoding F18's *intent*. The engine encodes the *artifact*. They agree everywhere except the paths that end an episode without writing anything — precisely where the bug lived, so the sim was correct by construction and blind to it.

The sim now advances the epoch only where the engine leaves a mark, and a human re-queue explicitly does not (a human editing labels writes no comment — which is the whole reason the strike must already have happened). All 46 existing scenarios still pass under the stricter model.

## Tests

Four new, each watched failing first, and each needing a **second executor**: a single executor beats its own stale claim by identity, which is the same masking that hid F18 until S32 raced two.

- `S39` — a rolled item is claimable by another executor on its next anchor
- `S39b` — a parked item a human re-queues is claimable by another executor at once
- engine loop: a second executor wins immediately on a rolled item, and on a hand-re-queued parked item
- engine loop: a losing claimant strikes too, so its claim does not own the next episode

Full suite: 1878 pass, 0 fail.

## Docs

- `DESIGN.md` §6.2 gains the strike beside F18's boundary rule.
- `SCENARIOS.md` gains S39 and the F24 row, placed in the F14–F18 lineage: a rule stated semantically, implemented over a subset of the paths that satisfy it.

## Deliberately not here

The `updated_at`-bump reclaim deferral — a losing claimant's own comment postpones the leash it depends on — is filed separately as #924. This change removes the common cause of those repeated losing claims; the general property survives it and wants its own fix.
